First, we express the given complex number in the form $z=x+y\text{i}.$ To do this, we remove $\text{i}$ from the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator of $z$ by the complex conjugate of the denominator, which is $1-\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{2}{1+\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{2(1-\text{i})}{(1+\text{i})(1-\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{2(1-\text{i})}{{1}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2(1-\text{i})}{1+1} \\  & =\frac{2(1-\text{i})}{2} \\  & =1-\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=1-\text{i},$ the magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

    

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=1$ is positive and $y=-1$ is negative, $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{-1}{1}| \\  & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡1 \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the complex number $z$ in polar form:

$$
z=\sqrt{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{4})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{4}))
$$
